core.store.note: P1-02 ships the 0600 file store with surfaced failures and store_status(); PKeyCore picks a platform store by default (Keychain, then Keystore, then the desktop keyring, else the file store). iOS, P5-05's Keychain store (core/store/keychain_store.gd over PKeyApple: device id and token AfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly, no access group); Android, P5-06's Keystore store (core/store/keystore_store.gd over PKeyAndroid: one AndroidKeyStore AES-256-GCM key per product, StrongBox where present, a lost key surfaced and re-enrolled); both migrate from the file store and surface failures as keyring-error. Desktop, SP-27's PKeyKeyringStore (core/store/keyring_store.gd), a port of UK-40's Kotlin KeyringStore: the token under service pkey:<product>, account device-token, verified writes (set, then read back), a write that cannot be verified kept in the 0600 file and surfaced (failed / store_error, status keyring-error), file-first reads, a file-store token moved into the keyring on the first read that verifies the move; the device id and cache stay in the files. Backends: macOS login keychain through PolarisKeyApple's desktop dylib (native/macos/build_apple.sh; SecureStore's login-keychain flavor, since the data-protection keychain needs an entitlement), Windows Credential Manager through pkey_win.dll's PKeyWinCredentialNative (python-keyring's target layout, LOCAL_MACHINE persistence), Linux Secret Service through secret-tool (secret on stdin, a deadline per call). Without the native piece (or with PKEY_DESKTOP_KEYRING=0) the store is the 0600 file and status() says keyring-unavailable with the reason. Web keeps the IndexedDB file store (degraded not-persistent). tests/suite_keyring.gd runs the contract over a fake backend, each backend over its fake, and, in native-desktop.yml's keyring job (PKEY_KEYRING_TESTS=1), the contract and the migration against the real keyring on macOS, Windows and Linux (Linux may record an N/A without a Secret Service). Shipping the plugins as an addon package is SP-G10.

core.copy.note: PKeyCopy (core/copy.gd, PolarisKey.core.copy, shared by every core) reads the generated PKeyCoreCopy with React's rule: message(code)/title(code) look up the error-code table, then the gate table, then the activation table; activation_message(kind)/activation_title(kind) read the activation table only; an unknown code reads COPY_FALLBACK naming it; {name} placeholders fill from params ({code} defaults to the code, an unfilled one is dropped); set_overrides() is the host layer. The kit's PKeyUiCopy reads it for every error_<code> key, its own overrides and translated kit lines first. tests/core/test_copy.gd covers every table, the fallback, placeholders, overrides and the activation-versus-code split. The .po generation from the catalogs is SP-G13.

core.backend.note: PolarisKey.backend (PKeyBackend): headers() (raw X-PKey-License and X-PKey-Device lines), headers_for(url) and request() send them only to PKeyOptions.backend_origins (exact, https except loopback); request() follows redirects by hand and checks every hop's origin before it is sent; the freshness pre-sync, one shared sync, one forced sync and retry on license_stale/license_invalid (at least 10 s apart), and not_entitled/sign_in_required as typed failures. tests/suite_backend.gd replays backend-matrix.json's client rows (the Godot SDK replays only the `client` section).

core.devicekeys.note: PKeyDeviceKeyStore (core/store/device_key_store.gd) over PKeyCurve25519 (core/crypto/curve25519.gd: ref10 Montgomery ladder and a mask-select fixed-base sign on PKeyEd25519's field code): a binary record in user://pkey/<product>/ written through FileAccess.open_encrypted_with_pass (passphrase from OS.get_unique_id plus a per-install salt; engine encryption can be turned off; best effort on mobile and consoles, where CC-26.7's native sealers replace it: PKeyRecordSealer (core/store/record_sealer.gd) with PKeyAppleSealer (Keychain AES-256-GCM key via PolarisKeyPlatform dk_*), PKeyAndroidSealer (Keystore via :platform's KeystoreSealer, ks_seal/ks_open/ks_destroy) and PKeyWinSealer (DPAPI, PKeyWinDpapiNative); the record file is PKSL||1||blob, protection() is <lane>-sealed, an unopenable sealed record is device-keys-unreadable and never replaced, a missing lane is unsupported, wipe() destroys the platform key; Linux has no sealer); every member answers a PKeyResult, so what the other stores throw is a code (device-keys-unreadable is never replaced and only wipe() resets it, unsupported is never reported for a bad record, device-keys-store-fault never reads as no keys); ensure/rotate/wipe run under a process mutex and a lock directory. PKeyDeviceKeys signs every pkey-proof/1 purpose and re-verifies it with PKeyDeviceProof (the strict verifier); PolarisKey.devices.register_keys sends PUT /devices/keys. tests/suite_devicekeys.gd: the CC-13 vectors, the store rules, every device-proof.json row and every valid purpose signed through the store. tests/suite_devicekeys_native.gd: selection and fallback, the sealed record, unreadable, fault, missing lane and wipe over a fake sealer, and the three lane adapters over fake natives.

license.manage.note: PX-W8: the device-limit result exposes manageUrl (validated), plus the return and key helpers.

config.resolve.note: OS.get_environment drops a leading U+FEFF from a value, so on a Godot host the two U+FEFF rows of config-matrix.json hold for the resolver, not for the process environment. A number's value is Godot's own reading, which is not correctly rounded, and a string value's \u0000 reads as U+FFFD (both WIRE-CONTRACT-V3 §10); verdicts are unaffected.

config.local.note: PKeyConfig.set_value/clear/clear_all/setting (S-17 §5.11's Godot names; set is Object's) write through the persisted PKeyConfigFileStore, check the value against the catalog entry's schema (type by value, not Variant: 40.0 is a valid integer), else the document value's JSON type, refuse an enforced or hidden key managed_by_admin, and emit config_changed once per write; setting(key) is a PKeyConfigSetting handle with changed(value, source) (tests/config/test_local.gd).

config.sync.note: PKeyConfig routes set_value/clear through Cloud Sync's machine while a person is signed in (the machine's order of refusals: invalid-options, then managed_by_admin), and PKeyConfigSetting.sync() answers local, pending or synced. The synced value sits in the local layer, below enforced and hidden (tests/suite_cloud_sync_settings.gd).

devices.fingerprint.note: PKeyFingerprint: per-platform readers as pure parsers over captured output, the capture on a WorkerThreadPool task once a session; the desktop device id hashes MachineGuid (Windows), IOPlatformUUID (macOS) and the rule-2 machine-id (Linux).

devices.report.note: The report also carries the Godot keys engine and outlet (the Worker bounds them; outlet is PKeyCore.reported_outlet()), and the updater's queued update events in updates (P6-03, P3-10).

devices.attest.note: P6-02: PolarisKey.devices.attest() (services/devices.gd) posts devices/attest/challenge, then devices/attest with an App Attest attestation (PKeyApple.app_attest over PolarisKeyPlatform's DCAppAttestService ops, clientDataHash = SHA-256 of the challenge's requestHash; the key id kept in the Keychain, re-attested with a fresh key when a reinstall, migration or restore killed it) or a standard Play Integrity token (PKeyAndroid.integrity_token over polaris-key-platform's play flavour, the requestHash verbatim, the cloud project number from the challenge or PKeyOptions.play_cloud_project_number). Unsupported runtime on desktop and web (and where App Attest does not run, the simulator); outlet on an iOS install that is not App Store or TestFlight, an Android install Google Play did not make or the direct plugin build, and a mobile build without the native plugin. Server codes are surfaced verbatim.

identity.oidc.note: Native Godot has no completion path for the OIDC redirect: it waits on the native redirect token route (I-15). The old /identity/auth/poll route is retired (the Worker no longer serves it) and was never a substitute. Until then P1-07's device-code sign-in is the path, and identity.sign_in.start({browser = true}) opens it in the system browser.

identity.devicecode.note: PolarisKey.identity (P1-07, I-10b.4): sign_in.start() returns a PKeySignInSession whose wait() polls on the server's cadence (outcome signal, cancel, reopen, typed PKeySignInOutcome), the opt-in confirm-identity step (choose, accept) and licence attach, the `identity` event, and a pure-GDScript QR encoder with PKeyQrRect for verification_uri_complete. On web it runs too (OS.shell_open becomes window.open; Worker CORS needed).

identity.devicelabel.note: PX-W13: PKeyDeviceLabel.normalize (UTF-32, one character per code point), PKeyOptions.device_name and send_device_name, the model-else-OS default, on sign_in.start, activation and registration; PKeySignInSession.device_name is the echo, and PKeySignInDialog shows it under the code. A per-call name wins; opting out is send_device_name = false (an exported String cannot be null).

identity.toggle.note: I-10b.4: a 404 on the device start is `service-unavailable` (detail.kind product, status 404) with the state kept; discovery's Identity-off answers it before any request. identity-disabled replayed.

identity.attach.note: I-10b.3: PolarisKey.identity.attach(confirm) over discovery's identity fragment: preview (detail kind confirm, nothing written), ok (token rotated and stored, subject, attached), a Worker refusal as a failure with its code and detail {kind: refused, status}, and service-unavailable without the endpoint; identity-attach and identity-attach-errors replayed. Device-code confirm (D-10): wait() returns choose only when the poll's confirm is attachable, otherwise the SDK answers no itself.

identity.account.note: I-10b.2: PolarisKey.identity.subject() (kept across restarts in the cache record), sign_out() (pre-sign-out hooks, POST signout, the token goes only on released: true) and open_account() over discovery's identity fragment (PKeyDiscovery.identity_from); a product without the endpoints answers service-unavailable and sign_out() keeps the license.deactivate() path. identity-subject-signout and discovery-identity transcripts replayed.

identity.redirect.web.note: I-10b.5: sign_in.start({channel = "redirect", redirect_uri}) builds the S256 authorize URL from discovery (PKeyIdentityRedirect) for a browser the host opens; session.complete(callback_url) checks the redirect URI, state and iss before anything is sent, then redeems the code at discovery's token endpoint (form body, product origin only). Single use; a refusal is a typed outcome and never wipes the token. Loopback, scheme and claimed-HTTPS redirects are I-15's; the licence choice (license_choice=app) is I-10b.6's.

identity.choice.note: I-10b.6: sign_in.start({channel = "redirect", license_choice = "app"}) settles complete() as the license_choice outcome (a grant, the choices) when discovery names the choice endpoints; PolarisKey.identity.choice.licenses / devices / complete / cancel (PKeyIdentityChoice) dial only those endpoints, send no bearer, return the Worker's refusals as PKeyChoiceResult values (retry_after_seconds, manage_url, sign_in_url, key_entries, the fresh view) and never print the grant. choice.primitives() are the Callables the sign-in form (ui/model/sign_in_session.gd) drives.

identity.exchange.note: Sign in with Apple on iOS and macOS, Credential Manager on Android (I-48); desktop Linux and Windows have none.

identity.keyentry.note: I-10b.1: activate_with_key() and enroll() return key-entry-limit (key_entries, manage_url) and license-owned (sign_in_url); key_entries on ok.

release.fetch.note: PolarisKey.release.fetch(target, to) (services/release.gd): a binary decision, a record or a record hash resolves to the verified record's payload artifact; the URL is discovery's distribution builds template; the bearer goes only to the control plane's origin and PKeyDownload drops it on a cross-origin redirect; a resume sends Range and If-Range with the payload's strong ETag; size and SHA-256 are checked before the part is renamed; a refusal surfaces the body's code. The updater's sidecar and APK paths share PKeyRelease.download_artifact. suite_transcripts maps releaseFetch and replays release-fetch-gated.json.

update.feeds.note: SP-26: PolarisKey.update.feed_url(kind, {channel, velopack_channel, build_id, arch}) (PKeyUpdate.feed_url_for) expands discovery's update.endpoints templates for appcast, winsparkle, velopack (the releases.<velopack_channel> file, or the UpdateManager feed directory without one), appInstaller and zsync; an absent channel is this build's or stable, an alias is rewritten through CHANNEL_ALIASES, each value is encodeURIComponent-encoded, and a missing template answers the typed unsupported (product). PKeyUpdater.feed_url (the native bridges' feeds) delegates to it; every feed-url-matrix.json row on the editor and the release template.

update.content.note: P4-24: core/feed.gd feed_content (packSets, packFloors, revocations parsed beside the claims with the token rule), distribution/decision.gd's content decision (select_pack_rows, composition, prestage, content-floor, revoked-content, packs; boot required only for revoked required content), services/update/flow.gd content steps 10-14; every feedContentCases and contentRows vector, stamp holds, on the editor and the release template.

update.driver.note: P3-10: one adapter per outlet kind (distribution/outlets/, PKeyOutletAdapter): store kinds open the https listing or PKeyOptions.update_page_url, platform kinds stay silent with their own message, web reloads, direct dispatches binary.method to the Sparkle, Velopack, WinSparkle or AppImageUpdate bridge (a missing plugin degrades to the build's download link from distribution.endpoints.builds), stages a verified sidecar .pck (updater/sidecar_swap.gd, Range resume through PKeyDownload) and restarts into it without --main-pack. Inert in the editor, headless runs and debug builds. P5-07: the bridges reach GDScript facades (addons/polaris_key/native/: PKeySparkle, PKeyVelopack, PKeyWinSparkle, PKeyStoreContext) over optional GDExtensions in sdks/godot/native/ (macOS Sparkle bridge; one Windows DLL with Velopack, WinSparkle and StoreContext; the Velopack launcher shim), each unsupported with runtime or dependency when unusable; ms-store hooks StoreContext in a Store MSIX. Under licensed or entitled delivery the Worker's package route redirects with a short-lived download ticket because Velopack drops Authorization on redirects (SP-09); a 401/403 download is retried once for a fresh ticket, and a second one answers unsupported (product). Suite native_desktop; the native-desktop workflow runs the updates end to end. Android (P5-06): the play and play-testing adapters drive Play In-App Updates through PKeyAndroid (native/pkey_android.gd over the PolarisKeyAndroid plugin and polaris-key-platform's play flavour: flexible or immediate by the decision's urgency, complete a downloaded update, silent while Play stages, the listing on any failure or a non-Play install); direct builds offer binary {method: native} through the apk bridge (available only on a direct-flavour build with the plugin): the direct adapter runs PKeyUpdater.install_apk (updater/apk_update.gd: the record's APK downloaded into user://, checked against the verified record's payload size and SHA-256, then PKeyAndroid.apk_install, the verified PackageInstaller self-update with the outcome journaled for the next launch), opening the download link only when the plugin answers unsupported.

update.bootguard.note: P3-10: updater/slots.gd (staged, current, previous and state.json under user://pkey/<product>/updates/) and updater/boot_guard.gd, run in PKeyBoot's GUARD: bootGuardAction over the host's own count, a restart before guard.done after a swap or a rollback, two failed boots roll back and record skipVersion, BOOT_OK_SECONDS and confirm_boot() per the stage-matrix v2 confirmation rows; every copy is read back from disk before a swap or rollback. update_downloaded, update_applied, update_confirmed and boot_rolled_back go out on devices/report's updates key (P6-03's boundedUpdates shape), queued in state.json until reported.

outlet.detect.note: distribution/outlet.gd PKeyOutlet.detect_outlet over distribution/outlet_signals.gd (Flatpak, snap, AppImage, Steam library and environment, itch receipt, macOS receipt and Mach-O leaf, Caskroom, Windows path conventions, Android getInstallSourceInfo through JavaClassWrapper (PKeyAndroid.install_source() reads the same facts, plus the initiator's full signer set, through the P5-06 plugin), web display mode); iOS reads AppDistributor (raced against 2 s, every launch), embedded.mobileprovision and ALTBundleIdentifier through the Apple plugin's facade (native/pkey_apple.gd, P5-05; no evidence without the plugin or before the launch read arrives); the Windows package reader is a hook that answers unavailable until a Windows native reader lands. PKeyCore.update_outlet() feeds the decision and PKeyCore.reported_outlet() the device report; PolarisKey.update.outlet() and detected() expose the result, as client.update.outlet and detected do in Node and Python.

packs.record.note: P4-08: core/release_record.gd applies the pack claims and pin.kind (PKeyPackClaims), packs/marker.gd verifies embedded-pack markers; the packs suite drives every packRecordCases and markerCases vector, the content stamps and packSetIdCases.

packs.revoke.note: P4-24: core/release_record.gd revocation_of / verify_revocation / newer_revocation (every revocationCases vector), packs/revocations.gd (the sibling content/revocations.json: written only with a first entry and revocationsStored first, re-verified on load, torn quarantined with relearn, unreadable writes nothing, the 256 cap, recover_state clears relearn) and the engine's pack-revoked.

packs.delegation.note: P4-26: core/release_record.gd verify_release_record (the delegated path, steps 13 and 16), verify_delegation (cached per hash and trust inputs), record_revoked; packs/dataonly.gd data_only_refusal with Amendment A1 (strict UTF-8 by hand, the text rule); the PackEngine fetches delegations only on the delegated surface (at most 16 per call), refuses non-data-only delegated installs with pack-not-data-only (before any payload fetch, while writing, and on a noop reuse), keeps the install's delegation and reloads through it, refuses releases under a revoked delegation (pack-revoked, detail delegation), never plans the GDDL route for delegated bytes and never mounts a delegated install; step 11 delegation relevance and the decision-input expansion in PKeyUpdateFlow; every delegationCases and dataOnlyCases vector on the editor and the release template.

packs.plan.note: P4-08: packs/select.gd (select_variant, plan_target, plan), a port of client-core; every plan-matrix.json (v2) row, variant case and target case on the editor and the release template; plan_target applies the P4-10 §2.5 chunk rule over the chunk index the engine stages (P4-11).

packs.index.files.note: P4-08: packs/files.gd (parse_files_index, check_paths, tree_digest) over PackedByteArray.decompress; every pathCases and filesIndexCases vector.

packs.index.chunks.note: P4-11: packs/chunks.gd parse_chunk_index / parse_chunk_index_bytes over PackedByteArray.decode_u32/decode_u16 (a u64 is two u32 reads composed and saturated at 2^53, never decode_u64), the zstd index through PackedByteArray.decompress with its exact size; every chunkIndexCases vector on the editor and the release template (4.4.1 and 4.7.2).

packs.apply.full.note: P4-08: packs/apply.gd apply_full (buffered: decompress cannot stream, so PKeyPacks.one_shot_budget can drop a too-large full before planning); applyCases on the editor and the release template.

packs.apply.file.note: P4-08: packs/apply.gd apply_file with the type-neutral container rebuild from gaps and blobs; a godot.pck installed without a kept index derives its files from its own PCK directory, so the next release can come by file.

packs.apply.chunk.note: P4-11: packs/chunks.gd apply_chunk (seed map, the planner's run rule, one single-range request per run, every fetched chunk decoded and verified, the repair pass) and chunk_range_fetch (Range bytes=o-e with If-Range on the bundle hash over HTTPClient with Accept-Encoding: identity, PKeyPackHttp.open_range pulling the body; only an exact 206 Content-Range, clipped at the object's end, and an ETag equal to the bundle hash are read, anything else falls back; no multi-range; Authorization dropped on a cross-origin redirect). PKeyPackEngine lists chunk in its strategies: seeds from this pack's installs, every other pack's active and previous installs and the embedded baselines, whose indexes are kept in <root>/index/<sha256> (backfilled after each ensure, re-verified at every use, collected with their installs); the target index staged before planning; the run bitmap in staging/<planId>/journal.json, re-hashed on resume; a refused range falls back, an interrupted one resumes at the next ensure. Delegated releases (trees) never plan chunk. Every chunk applyCases vector on the editor and the release template.

packs.apply.delta.note: P4-08: zstd --patch-from frames decoded by the ENGINE's own GDDL delta decoder (a PACK_FILE_DELTA helper pack over a private-namespace prefix: a trailer appended to the installed store pack and truncated back, or a copy host), after the window check; advertised (zstd-patch-from) only on the pinned engines PKeyPackZstd.PATCH_FROM_ENGINES (4.6, 4.7) whose start-up probe decodes. On the 4.4 floor the planner never chooses a delta and the corpus's decode cases fail closed (delta-apply-failed).

packs.delta.feed.note: P4-31: core/feed.gd feed_content reads the deltas menu (plans/P4-29.md §2.2: both caps and both uniqueness rules counting dropped entries, a forward scope dropped alone, integer claims through PKeyClaims.is_wire_integer); packs/select.gd with_feed_deltas; PKeyPackEngine.feed_deltas (PKeyPacks wires the menu of the feed the last update check committed, else the cached committed feed) tries at most one feed-offered delta per install, falls back after a 404 or any verdict, journals feedDelta and merges it again on resume, and re-plans a journal whose delta is unknown. Godot has no native payload port, so there is no native path. Every feedContentCases deltas check, feedDeltaCases and feedDeltaApplyCases vector on the editor and the release template.

packs.state.note: P4-08: packs/state.gd and PKeyPackEngine (client-core's PackEngine) over PKeyPackStorage in user://pkey (staging, store/<sha256>.pck, trees/<sha256>/, content/state.json): journal, Range/If-Range resume, read-back before every rename, torn-state quarantine with its saved snapshot, unreadable-state refusal, deferred installs, GC roots, embedded baselines from res://pkey_packs/; packSetId on devices/report; the shared boot guard rolls a failed pack set back with the binary and holds each rolled-back record (held, with a count) until the stamp pins another (pack-rolled-back on ensure).

packs.handlers.note: P4-08: PolarisKey.update.packs.register_handler; files.tree (hot, versioned directory plus pointer swap) and godot.pck (restart; the header and directory checks before commit and mount: normal paths only, resources judged by content (RSRC/text head; RSCC decompressed, bounded, then scanned, P4-27), remap/import targets and uid_cache.bin entries inside the pack; files.tree outputs content-scanned too; mounted in mountOrder, one per frame after the first frame, replace_files=true, from content-addressed paths) built in. P4-16: godot.zip, data.json and l10n.table built in, audio.bank and custom.* registered by the game; a tree handler's base check_tree runs the v1 tree rule (PKeyPck.tree_check) before the type's check_payload, so a custom.* handler never relaxes it; a type refusal is pack-type-check-failed (the detail token in the message, the path in detail.path).

packs.provides.note: P4-20: packs/provides.gd (PKeyPackProvides): provides_of reads a verified record's reserved record-level provides (absent or unusable provides nothing); PolarisKey.update.packs.is_available(content_id) answers from the running set (embedded baselines included) and pack_for(content_id, targets) (a coroutine) from the stamp's pins or a packs decision's targets, reading only records (an install's verified record, else fetched by hash and verified as preflight does); an unentitled pack never answers.

packs.type.godot.zip.note: P4-16: packs/godot_zip_handler.gd (PKeyGodotZipHandler, built in): a stored zip read from its bytes (end record closing the file, no comment, ZIP64, encryption or data descriptor, STORE only, local headers agreeing, no overlap, normal unique paths), then the godot.pck admission list over handler.prefixes; stored as store/<sha256>.zip (named by its leading bytes) and mounted by mount() with the godot.pck packs.

packs.type.l10n.table.note: P4-16: packs/l10n_table_handler.gd and l10n_parse.gd (built in): PO, CSV and JSON tables by plain parsers (format by content, never extension), BCP-47 locale matched to the variant; activation adds code-built Translation objects to the TranslationServer and a swap, rollback or deactivation removes the previous install's; plural forms through Translation on 4.6+, singular only before; no .translation load, no Plural-Forms evaluation.

packs.type.data.json.note: P4-16: packs/data_json_handler.gd (built in): every file strict JSON (PKeyJson) with an object at the top, whatever its name; format versions the host lists (default [1]); documents(pack_id) and on_activate/on_deactivate.

packs.type.audio.bank.note: P4-16: packs/audio_bank_handler.gd (PKeyAudioBankHandler, registered by the game with its middleware, version and reload/unload callables): bank.json's middleware and major.minor against the host's; hot when reload is given, else restart; banks never mounted.

packs.type.ml.model.note: P4-16: Godot has no ML runtime; a game that adds one registers its own handler.

packs.transport.apple.note: P5-08: packs/transport_apple_ba.gd (PKeyPackAppleBaTransport) over P5-05's PKeyApple: the level's asset pack <pack>-c<contentApi> (dots to hyphens), files under pkey/<asset pack>/ resolved with url(for:) every call and never persisted, ensure_packs with progress forwarded; the engine verifies the marker and the payload or treeDigest against the signed record before activation, floats a later release at boot, and plans a carried pack only through the platform (plan-transport-unsupported while it is unavailable). Stub-proven in suite_transports against the fake PolarisKeyApple native; the TestFlight device run is the owner's (P5-08 owner checklist). macOS answers Unsupported (runtime): no work package owns a macOS binding (P5-05 Out).

packs.transport.play.note: P5-08: packs/transport_play_pad.gd (PKeyPackPlayPadTransport) over P5-06's PKeyAndroid: the Play asset pack named by the pack id with dots and hyphens as underscores, its assetsPath re-read every launch (pkey/ or a pkey#tcf_* directory), pack_fetch to COMPLETED, a host confirm_hook before Play's dialog for WAITING_FOR_WIFI / REQUIRES_USER_CONFIRMATION, Unsupported (outlet) on the direct build; a delivered copy must be the pinned release (Play asset packs ship with the bundle). Stub-proven in suite_transports against the fake PolarisKeyAndroid plugin; the internal-track device run is the owner's (P5-08 owner checklist).

packs.transport.steam.note: P5-08: packs/transport_steam.gd (PKeyPackSteamTransport) over GodotSteam when present: <install dir>/pkey_packs/<pack id>/ read only (never written), DLC packs gated on isDLCInstalled and installed with installDLC / dlc_installed, build id and beta branch for diagnostics, Unsupported (dependency) without GodotSteam; a content-only build's later release floats at boot. Stub-proven in suite_transports against a fake GodotSteam; the test-branch device run is the owner's (P5-08 owner checklist).

packs.transport.msix.note: No work package owns an MSIX transport for Godot (program README §9).

packs.transport.flatpak.note: No work package owns a Flatpak transport for Godot (program README §9).

ui.stages.note: PKeyStages (core/stages.gd) replays every stage-matrix.json row, probe, guard and confirm case; PKeyBoot drives every row through PolarisKey.boot() with a scripted host (suite_boot).

ui.kit.note: P1-10's v1 kit: PKeyBoot, gate, activation panel, sign-in dialog with QR, offline activation, settings panel, status banner, update prompt, entitlement badge and dev-menu section, pinned as structural snapshots and centred at five window sizes (suite_ui); responsive (landscape and portrait layouts, a screen scale, densities, the safe area) with a 4 px spacing scale, layout roles and a type scale in every stock theme, laid out across the resolution matrix (tests/ui/matrix.gd: ten sizes and five stretch settings, four looks, en/de/ja) with no overflow, overlap, clipped text or unscannable QR code (suite_ui_matrix; tools/ui_matrix renders it); the Polaris Key look by default (ink primary or the product's accent, 3 px focus ring) with a native look over the game's theme (ui_branding none) and an optional Powered-by badge (PKeyOptions.ui_*, PKeyUiTheme; suite_brand); a pad-driven cold start, number settings by left and right, full-bleed phone screens with docked actions and no QR code on a phone (suite_ui_matrix). The UI-KITS §4.1 components the kit lacked are in too: PKeyDeviceList (Devices: 64 px rows, form-factor glyphs, rename and remove in place), PKeyLicenseChoice (LicenseChoice: origin, term, seat meter, current and full tags, one primary), PKeyAccountTab (AccountAndLicense: grouped rows, danger Sign out; also the Account section of PKeySettingsPanel), PKeyToast (a 6 s timer, at most two actions, persisting errors, reach without taking the focus) and PKeyUpdateProgress (a counted bar and its states), each following its ui-core model state for state (suite_ui_components); the pack progress UI is P4-08's.

ui.kit.manage.note: PX-W8: the activation panel shows Replace a device on device-limit, or a QR when a joypad is the only input (suite_ui).

ui.kit.account.note: I-10b.7: the sign-in dialog drives identity.sign_in.start (a PKeySignInSession) and the account tab and gate sign out through identity.sign_out (I-10b.4, I-10b.3); the activation panel's License in another account step reads "Sign in to that account" (signin.key.ownedSignIn, UKV7-godot, KF-godot), and the gate toasts "Signed in as {name} · {tier} license" (signin.desktop.toast). PKeyLicenseChoiceController stays a view helper. The dialog's confirm step carries the attach toggle (session.accept) (suite_ui).

ui.kit.keyentry.note: I-10b.7: the key-entry-limit step shows "{used} of {limit} key entries used" (signin.key.meter) from the activation result's key_entries, Sign in, "Add it in Polaris Locker" (a QR with its caption when a joypad is the only input) and Use a different key; a key that works toasts "{left} key entries left" (signin.key.entriesLeftShort) (suite_ui).

commerce.receipt.note: PolarisKey.commerce (services/commerce.gd, P6-01): binding() (the licence's purchase binding — P5-05 PKeyApple's appAccountToken, godot-google-play-billing's obfuscatedAccountId, GodotSteam's getAuthTicketForWebApi identity — and the mapped store products) and claim(store, payload) for the StoreKit JWS, the Play purchase token or the Steam web-API ticket; the Worker verifies with the store and grants the licence flag. hidden_here() applies App Store 3.1.3(b) on Apple outlets. suite_commerce and the commerce-claim transcript (suite_transcripts).

sync.scenarios.note: core/sync/cloud_sync_machine.gd replays every sync-scenarios.json scenario with no skip list, and sync_routes.gd the settingCases (tests/suite_sync_scenarios.gd; the corpus is read through the strict parser, ints stay ints).

sync.settings.note: PolarisKey.cloud_sync (PKeyCloudSync: status(), flush(), the cloudSync event) over services/cloud_sync/ (host, sealed state file, transport with no redirects, a 15 s timeout and an 8 MiB cap, the codec port) and the machine. Sign-out runs flush, machine sign-out, ring forget, purge in that order and stops when the ring cannot forget (suite_cloud_sync_host, suite_cloud_sync_settings). The journal is sealed by the platform lane or the engine-encrypted file keyed from the device id; with neither a sealer nor a device id it is not written.

sync.keyring.note: PolarisKey.keyring (PKeySyncRing, over core/sync: HKDF and HMAC on the engine, AES-256-GCM as an AESContext ECB keystream with GDScript GHASH (at most 64 KiB per call: a setting is at most 8 KiB, files stay native-only), RFC 9180 mode_base over the device key store's dh for open and an ephemeral X25519 key for seal): create(), unlock() (opens this device's wrap through the store's dh, so the agreement key never leaves it), wrap_to()/remove_wrap(), set_recovery_code()/recover(), reset()/adopt()/adopt_root()/open_adopted(), accept_ring_change(confirmed), attach(listener) and the codec. The first root pins {ring_id, epoch, root_kid} per product; a served ring that differs answers ring-changed and is never opened. The root is also kept in one record used only while it matches the pin: sealed by the platform lane where one exists (Keychain, Keystore, DPAPI), else the engine-encrypted file keyed from the device id (a weaker store than the OS keychains, obfuscation against a casual copy), or memory only (web without a persistent user://). forget() drops the root and the pin and runs from the sign-out hook. Every type holding key material prints as redacted. suite_sync_vectors (hkdf, envelope, blind, canonicalJson, hpkeAnchor, wrap, recovery and adopt cases), suite_sync_ring and the keyring-* transcripts in suite_transcripts.
